pullRequest.title: perf(telemetry): stamp every deck-load row with the conditions it was measured under (PERF-R7)

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [BLOCKING] Close every started load span**

When preparation succeeds but the later swap rejects—such as the existing direct-engine activation race where playback starts during a load—execution throws from `_withDeckSwap` without reaching either `recordDeckLoad` call. The span opened here therefore remains indefinitely in flight, causing every subsequent deck-load row to report `solo=0` until the span is eventually evicted; ensure post-preparation failures also close and record the span.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L35-L36](https://github.com/private_owner/music-dj-tools/blob/bec44a183c9e45185d78ccb8927c27fe06614056/AGENTS.md#L35-L36)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

FIXED in d5cb3737e. The most valuable of the three, because it corrupts the INSTRUMENT rather than the feature.

Confirmed exactly as described: `_withDeckSwap` sits outside the try that records the row, so a swap rejection reached neither `recordDeckLoad` call. The consequence is worse than a missing row -- every later load reported `solo=0` until the 16-deep window evicted the leaked span, i.e. a contention label that is WRONG while looking exactly like a measurement. That is the failure mode `.claude/rules/verification.md` exists to forbid, and it would have quietly poisoned the very readings this PR adds.

Closed with a `.catch` on the swap promise: it stamps `stages.total`, files a `deck-load-fail-swap` row (which closes the span) and rethrows, so the caller's error handling is unchanged.

Attached to the promise rather than wrapped in `try`/`catch` deliberately: a try block would have re-indented roughly 90 lines for a 5-line fix, and `audio-engine.svelte.ts` is at its `file_size.max_frontend` ceiling with no room to pay for the noise. Two unrelated multi-line imports collapse to single lines to fund the 5 lines; the file lands at 4069, exactly main's level.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [BLOCKING] Preserve the pressure sample's real age**

When a pressure response is delayed, this records `receivedAtMs` only after the response body arrives, so `pressure_age_ms` omits the response/event-loop delay and can label an old sample as fresh. Overlapping polls compound this because an older request that completes last unconditionally overwrites a newer snapshot; retain request/sample timing and reject out-of-order completions before storing the evidence.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L35-L36](https://github.com/private_owner/music-dj-tools/blob/bec44a183c9e45185d78ccb8927c27fe06614056/AGENTS.md#L35-L36)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

FIXED in d5cb3737e. Both halves were real and both are fixed.

**The age.** `receivedAtMs` was stamped after the body finished parsing, so the round trip and the event-loop wait were erased from the number whose entire job is to say how stale the reading is. The field is now `requestedAtMs`, stamped BEFORE the fetch. That means the age can only ever OVERSTATE how stale a sample is, which is the safe direction for a number a reader uses to decide whether to trust the row beside it -- the opposite of what it did before.

**The ordering.** Also correct, and it is the nastier half: the 10s timer does not wait for the previous request, so a slow poll completing after a fast one overwrote the newer reading with the older and walked the cache BACKWARDS in time while every field still looked valid. `storeMachinePressure` now rejects any snapshot that is not strictly newer, ordered on the request instant since that is when each sample was asked for. It returns whether it stored, so a caller (and a test) can tell a rejected late arrival from an accepted one rather than both looking like success.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [BLOCKING] Replace mocked machine-condition tests**

The new sampler suite replaces production OS calls with `monkeypatch` functions, and the accompanying cache/browser suites similarly inject fake samplers and `fetch` responses. That violates the repository's fail-closed no-mocks contract and allows these tests to pass without exercising the production command, parser, endpoint, and client path; use captured real payloads through a production parser plus real-path integration coverage instead.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L125-L129](https://github.com/private_owner/music-dj-tools/blob/bec44a183c9e45185d78ccb8927c27fe06614056/AGENTS.md#L125-L129)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

PARTLY FIXED, PARTLY REBUTTED in d5cb3737e. The gap you name is real and is now closed; two of the specifics are not accurate about this diff, and I would rather say so than silently rewrite working tests.

**Rebutted: the parser was never mocked.** `test_probe_machine_conditions.py` feeds CAPTURED REAL `vm_stat` output (trimmed from this Mac's actual output, dated in the file) through `native._vm_stat_free_mb`, which IS the shipped production parser. Substituting `run_text` is the mechanism for delivering a captured payload deterministically -- it is the thing you are asking for, not a stand-in for it. Replacing it with 'captured real payloads through a production parser' would be a no-op rename.

**Rebutted: the endpoint already had real coverage.** `test_pressure_route_answers_over_real_http` and `test_pressure_route_does_not_leak_process_detail` drive the real route through `TestClient` with nothing injected, and assert the available/unavailable disjunction plus the response allowlist.

**Fixed: the production COMMAND was genuinely untested.** Nothing ran the real `vm_stat` and `sysctl`. Five additions:

- `test_the_real_sampler_reports_finite_numbers_or_nothing_at_all` -- the real `read_machine_pressure()`, unpatched
- `test_the_real_load_average_is_a_plausible_reading_not_a_placeholder` -- zero rejected as an error signature, since a silent failure returns 0.0 and reads as an idle machine
- `test_the_real_sampler_runs_and_omits_what_it_cannot_read` -- real `machine_metrics()`, asserting absent-not-None
- `test_the_real_vm_stat_parse_is_a_positive_free_memory_or_no_key`
- `a real deck load stamps the real machine conditions` (boot-burst lane) -- the whole browser path with nothing injected: real engine, real endpoint, real poller, real deck load, asserting the row carries `solo=1 concurrent_loads=1` and a finite reading or none. Verified passing.

All assert the CONTRACT, not values, because the value is whatever the machine is doing and CI is not this Mac. The contract is what a regression breaks: a field is a finite number or it is ABSENT, never present-and-zero.

**Kept: the injected samplers in the cache suite.** Those reach branches a real machine cannot be asked to produce on demand -- a sampler that raises `OSError`, one that returns nothing, one whose extra keys the allowlist must drop. Deleting them would delete the only coverage of the failure paths, which is the opposite of fail-closed. The real-path tests above now sit beside them so both halves are covered.

One caveat I will state rather than let you find: the boot-burst lane is a MEASUREMENT lane and is not wired into CI, so that e2e is reproducible on demand (`just boot-burst-bench`) rather than gating. Say the word if you want it moved into the rekordbox gate instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [BLOCKING] Bind completion to its own load span**

Fresh evidence beyond the earlier leaked-span report is the supported direct-engine overlap path in `performance-controls.spec.ts`, which starts two `engine.load(4, ...)` calls concurrently. Because `_closeSpan` selects the newest open span by deck rather than the span created by this invocation, whichever same-deck load finishes first closes the other load's interval; if other decks were concurrently loading before the second load started, the first row can underreport `concurrent_loads`, and the later row uses the wrong widened interval. Return a span-bound completion handle or ID from `beginDeckLoad` so each row closes its own interval.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L35-L36](https://github.com/private_owner/music-dj-tools/blob/d5cb3737e5c24dfeb675bc168536bcf479821007/AGENTS.md#L35-L36)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [BLOCKING] Retain in-flight spans when bounding history**

When one deck load remains slow while sixteen later loads start on independent deck scopes, this unconditional tail slice evicts the still-running span along with old completed history. Subsequent rows then cannot see that active load and can incorrectly report `solo=1`; when the slow load eventually finishes, its synthesized span also cannot recover the discarded overlap history. Bound only completed spans, while retaining every in-flight span until it is closed.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L219-L223](https://github.com/private_owner/music-dj-tools/blob/d5cb3737e5c24dfeb675bc168536bcf479821007/AGENTS.md#L219-L223)
